# Siri AI availability: devices, EU access and the waitlist after launch


By OpenTools Team


Siri AI has begun rolling out. Here are the supported devices, beta waitlist steps, EU platform exceptions and the cloud‑limit details Apple has not specified.


Apple began rolling out Siri AI in English on **September 14, 2026** , but installing the new operating system does not complete the process of getting the assistant. Device eligibility, language and account settings, regional restrictions, and a separate beta enrollment step all affect access. Apple’s[launch announcement](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant-is-here/) establishes the release date; its[activation instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127893) add the practical catch: users join a waitlist, with variable waiting times, before Siri AI downloads automatically. Someone who has finished updating can therefore still be waiting for the feature itself.


The distinction matters because “supports Siri AI” also does not mean “supports every new voice feature.” Apple has a broader device list for the assistant and a narrower one for its advanced on‑device model. The useful starting point is the capability that is missing, followed by the device, region and activation requirements attached to it. Those are separate questions, and treating them as one compatibility test can send a user toward an unnecessary hardware purchase or a settings change that cannot resolve a regional restriction.


##


The supported‑device list has two tiers


For the Siri AI beta, Apple lists the following combinations in its[current requirements](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148218) and[setup guide](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127893) . These describe supported hardware, not a promise that enrollment has completed on every eligible device. Both the device language and Siri language must be English at launch. Apple says French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish support is coming in **October 2026** ; that is the announced next stage, rather than a list of languages already enabled for this beta.[September rollout details](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant-is-here/)


Scroll sideways to see all columns.


Device Siri AI beta requirements Important boundary


iPhone iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, iPhone 16 models or later, or iPhone Air; iOS 27 The ordinary iPhone 15 and 15 Plus are outside this list.


iPad iPad mini with A17 Pro, or an M1‑or‑later iPad; iPadOS 27 Being able to install iPadOS 27 alone does not establish eligibility.


Mac MacBook Neo with A18 Pro, or an M1‑or‑later Mac; macOS 27 Golden Gate Check the chip, not just the Mac’s product name.


Apple Vision Pro Any Apple Vision Pro; visionOS 27 The separate advanced‑voice requirement is narrower.


Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Ultra 2 or later, or SE 3; watchOS 27 An Apple Intelligence‑enabled iPhone must be nearby.


Expressive voices and advanced dictation belong to the higher hardware tier. Apple’s launch footnote names iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and iPhone Duo; qualifying iPads need M4 or later **and at least 12GB of unified memory** , while qualifying Macs need M3 or later **and at least 12GB** . The model and expressive voices also reach Vision Pro with M5. These requirements should not be used to exclude an otherwise supported device from the base assistant. Apple separately excludes users under 13 from Siri AI.[Hardware and age footnotes](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant-is-here/)


##


A compatible device can still be waiting for activation


After updating, Apple directs users to **Settings → Siri → Try Siri AI (Beta)** . If Siri is off, it must first be turned on. The subsequent setup covers voice selection, voice enrollment and privacy settings; completing it adds the user to the waitlist. Apple gives no fixed waiting time in that guide and says the download starts automatically when the wait ends. That makes an on‑screen enrollment state more useful than someone else’s report of receiving access quickly. The guide describes a process, not a universal delivery deadline.[Apple’s activation sequence](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127893)


There is also a local preparation requirement. Apple’s broader[Intelligence setup document](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115) specifies on‑device storage needs, including up to 8GB for other Apple Intelligence‑enabled iPhone, iPad and Mac models and up to 14GB for the listed advanced‑model configurations. It says changing Siri’s language can interrupt availability until the new language finishes downloading and matches the device language. Check free storage and the two language settings before interpreting an unfinished download as a device‑support decision. Storage preparation, beta admission and hardware eligibility describe different stages of the same setup.


##


EU availability depends on the platform


For EU residents, Siri AI is unavailable on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS at launch. Apple’s support documentation explicitly allows it on **macOS 27 Golden Gate and visionOS 27** , provided the Apple Account region is in the EU and both device and Siri languages are English. An eligible Mac and an eligible iPhone can therefore have different outcomes under the same regional account. Switching between those devices does not establish that one has failed to update correctly.[Siri AI regional requirements](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148218)


The restriction is also narrower than a blanket absence of Apple Intelligence in Europe. Apple lists other new features, including photo editing, Image Playground and browsing features, as available on supported EU devices. Its Siri‑specific guide says the new assistant will not currently work when the Apple Account region is mainland China; the broader Intelligence document adds separate conditions involving where a device was purchased and, for devices purchased elsewhere, location and account region. Keep those policies attached to the feature being checked, rather than treating a successful unrelated AI feature as proof that Siri must be available.[Apple Intelligence availability](https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115) ·[Siri AI account‑region rule](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127893)


##


Apple has described cloud limits without publishing a fixed allowance


The limit policy has a timing gap. Apple’s September 14 launch notice says server‑backed features are subject to daily limits, while its dedicated[usage‑limit guide](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127901) , dated September 9, describes implementation as a future step. That guide says access can depend on the feature, request complexity, demand and policy, and that a feature becomes available again after a timeout. Neither page provides a fixed Siri request allowance or a price for expanded access. The supported takeaway is that Apple has announced a variable limit policy; the documents do not establish a single quota every user can expect today.


Scroll sideways to see all columns.


Access question What Apple has published What remains unspecified


Will all Siri requests count the same way? Limits can vary with feature and request complexity. A public per‑request accounting schedule.


What happens after a limit? The affected feature may be restricted until reset; other device features can still be used. One universal reset time or daily Siri allowance.


Can users pay for more? Increased access is planned for a fee. A Siri price, purchase date or guaranteed allowance.


The[usage terms](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148587) allow feature limits to change and distinguish a restriction on one feature from continued use of others. That matters when diagnosing a failed request: a cloud‑access restriction is a different condition from losing device eligibility. Apple’s limits guide also discusses iCloud+ camera allowances for Home features, but those figures describe cameras, not Siri request quotas. They should not be turned into a claim that buying a particular iCloud+ plan currently guarantees a specified Siri allowance.[Feature‑specific limit details](https://support.apple.com/en-us/127901)


##


On‑device processing does not make the assistant entirely offline


Apple describes an architecture combining local processing with **Private Cloud Compute** , which can use larger server models for requests. Its privacy claim is that data handled through that system is not stored or made accessible to Apple or others. That is a description of how cloud requests are handled, not a claim that every request stays on the device. A phone can support an advanced local model while still using services with separate availability or usage conditions.[Apple’s processing and privacy explanation](https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence/)


For someone trying to get Siri AI working, the order of checks is consequently practical: establish base device support, confirm the platform’s regional and language rules, then inspect enrollment and download progress. Once the assistant is active, distinguish an unavailable advanced voice option from a restricted server‑backed request. That sequence will not make a waitlist move faster or remove an announced regional exclusion, but it identifies which published requirement actually bears on the problem—and whether replacing hardware would address it at all.
